title: Python SDK async-iterator cookbook: ergonomic streamed structured outputs, granular retries & backpressure
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Deliver an ergonomic set of primitives and example recipes for consuming streamed structured outputs from the Python SDK. Focus areas: async iterator API surface, explicit backpressure hooks for consumer-driven flow control, deterministic retry semantics for mid-stream failures, and a cookbook of common patterns (sync wrappers, chunk-aggregation, resumable parses).
acceptance_criteria: Async generator API that yields typed Pydantic/dataclass models for each logical output chunk
Clear backpressure mechanism (consumer-controlled prefetch/acksize) documented and unit-tested
Retry semantics documented and implemented: idempotent restart where possible, configurable resume points for chunked outputs
Three cookbook examples: async consumer, sync convenience iterator, and resumable-download pattern
End-to-end integration tests that validate semantics against a streaming test harness and GH Actions matrix (py38/py39/py310)
Docs and code samples added to SDK docs and example repo; API stable enough for 0.28.0 release toggles
design_notes: Goal: reduce boilerplate for users parsing structured JSON-lines and protobuf-framed tokens while exposing minimal knobs for backpressure
We prefer an async generator (async for) as the primary surface and provide a thin synchronous wrapper for sync apps (iterator that drives an event loop in a background thread)
Typed hydration will use existing Pydantic models where available, with optional dataclass conversion helpers for users who prefer dataclasses
Make retry policy pluggable: built-in BackoffWithResume (best-effort to resume using server-provided continuation tokens) + simple RestartOnFailure for non-resumable streams
Careful about memory: implement chunk windowing and max-buffer-size guardrails to avoid OOM on fast producers
decisions: Primary API: client.stream(..., model=..., parse_as=MySchema) -> AsyncIterator[MySchema]
Backpressure controls: prefetch (int) + ack() hook implemented on iterator object to allow consumer-driven pacing
Retry default: RestartOnFailure with 3 attempts; enable BackoffWithResume for servers that return continuation tokens
Do not change existing sync streaming endpoints; provide sync wrapper in examples and a convenience helper in sdk.streaming.sync_utils
Parsing: stream parser will emit partial hydration events for nested objects; final hydration occurs once logical message complete
implementation_plan: Spike: implement prototype async iterator + test harness (done 2025-01-22)
Core: implement iterator object with prefetch/ack + integration with existing HTTP streaming transport (2 weeks)
Parser: integrate streaming JSON-lines parser and typed hydration path (pydantic & dataclass) (1 week)
Retries: add pluggable retry adapter with resume token support; write unit tests for resume behavior (1 week)
Docs & cookbook: write three consumer examples, update SDK docs, and add migration notes (3 days)
Canary & release: land behind feature-flag and dogfood at Redwood apps; roll out in python-sdk-0.28.0
